title: TT-Lang cheat sheet for a kernel

roots.hardware: the tt-lang package installed for the chip (1.1.6): what compiles
roots.tree: the tt-lang checkout's compiler package (newer than the package)
roots.sim: the checkout's simulator (accepts more than the chip's compiler)

intro: Each tag says what is known. [compiles on hardware]: an elementwise kernel built from these calls ran on the chip. [hardware signature only]: the signature is in the hardware package and no compile was shown. [simulator only]: the simulator accepts it and the hardware package does not. A simulator pass does not show a kernel compiles for the chip. Do not import ttl or ttnn to look things up. `python3 stage_tools.py cheat NAME` prints one entry where the tool exists.

entries.name: ttl.operation
entries.notes: Decorator for the host function. It takes ttnn tensors and writes the output tensor in place. Define the dataflow buffers and the three threads inside it. grid='full' uses every node; a tuple such as (1, 1) is one node. Older text says @ttl.kernel: that name does not exist in the package.
entries.evidence: issue 205 and docs/run-logs/2026-10-28-granite-mamba2-real-port.md: an elementwise kernel built from these calls compiled and ran on the chip with tt-lang 1.1.6

entries.name: ttl.compute
entries.notes: The math thread. It waits on input buffers, reserves the output buffer and calls store. One per kernel.
entries.evidence: issue 205 and docs/run-logs/2026-10-28-granite-mamba2-real-port.md: an elementwise kernel built from these calls compiled and ran on the chip with tt-lang 1.1.6

entries.name: ttl.datamovement
entries.notes: A data-movement thread: it copies tensor slices into buffers (reader) or buffers into tensors (writer). Two per kernel.
entries.evidence: issue 205 and docs/run-logs/2026-10-28-granite-mamba2-real-port.md: an elementwise kernel built from these calls compiled and ran on the chip with tt-lang 1.1.6

entries.name: ttl.make_dataflow_buffer_like
entries.notes: A buffer in L1 that takes dtype and layout from a tensor. shape is the block in tiles. The keyword is block_count; buffer_factor does not exist. One producer thread and one consumer thread per buffer, and both loop the same number of times.
entries.evidence: issue 205 and docs/run-logs/2026-10-28-granite-mamba2-real-port.md: an elementwise kernel built from these calls compiled and ran on the chip with tt-lang 1.1.6

entries.name: ttl.grid_size
entries.notes: The grid's size as (columns, rows). Use it at the top of the operation to split the work.
entries.evidence: issue 205 and docs/run-logs/2026-10-28-granite-mamba2-real-port.md: an elementwise kernel built from these calls compiled and ran on the chip with tt-lang 1.1.6

entries.name: ttl.node
entries.notes: This node's coordinates, called inside a thread. Split rows or columns of tiles over nodes with it and guard the tail with `if row < row_tiles`.
entries.evidence: issue 205 and docs/run-logs/2026-10-28-granite-mamba2-real-port.md: an elementwise kernel built from these calls compiled and ran on the chip with tt-lang 1.1.6

entries.name: DataflowBuffer.wait
entries.usage: with a_dfb.wait() as a_blk, out_dfb.reserve() as o_blk: o_blk.store(a_blk)
entries.notes: Consumer side: blocks until a block is ready; the block is released when the with block ends. In the compute thread this is how input is read.
entries.evidence: issue 205 and docs/run-logs/2026-10-28-granite-mamba2-real-port.md: an elementwise kernel built from these calls compiled and ran on the chip with tt-lang 1.1.6

entries.name: DataflowBuffer.reserve
entries.usage: with a_dfb.reserve() as blk: ttl.copy(a_in[0:2, 0:1], blk).wait()
entries.notes: Producer side: blocks until there is room; the block is pushed when the with block ends. The reader reserves, the compute thread reserves the output.
entries.evidence: issue 205 and docs/run-logs/2026-10-28-granite-mamba2-real-port.md: an elementwise kernel built from these calls compiled and ran on the chip with tt-lang 1.1.6

entries.name: TensorBlock.store
entries.notes: Writes a block expression into an output block reserved from a buffer. Elementwise operators (+, -, *, /) work on blocks of the same shape.
entries.evidence: issue 205 and docs/run-logs/2026-10-28-granite-mamba2-real-port.md: an elementwise kernel built from these calls compiled and ran on the chip with tt-lang 1.1.6

entries.name: ttl.copy
entries.notes: Copies a tensor slice into a block, or a block into a tensor slice (slices are in tiles). It returns a handle; wait on it before the block ends. A slice that does not match the buffer's block shape fails to compile.
entries.evidence: issue 205 and docs/run-logs/2026-10-28-granite-mamba2-real-port.md: an elementwise kernel built from these calls compiled and ran on the chip with tt-lang 1.1.6

entries.name: ttl.math.reduce_sum
entries.notes: Sum over the grid dimension in dims (-1 is across a row of tiles). The result keeps one value per row in column 0 of each tile: spread it back with ttl.math.broadcast. There is no shape argument in the hardware package.

entries.name: ttl.math.reduce_max
entries.notes: Maximum over dims, same shape rules as reduce_sum (softmax).

entries.name: ttl.math.broadcast
entries.notes: Spreads a reduced block (a column of values) back across dims to the given shape; the way to multiply a row by its own statistic.

entries.name: ttl.matmul
entries.notes: Tile matmul of two blocks: (m, k) tiles by (k, n) tiles. Accumulating over k means looping over k blocks and adding the partial results.

entries.name: ttl.math.transpose
entries.notes: Transposes a block of tiles.

entries.name: ttl.math.fill
entries.notes: A block of one value; use it for scalar constants in an expression, such as epsilon.

entries.name: ttl.math.typecast
entries.notes: Changes the dtype of a block.

entries.name: ttl.math.rsqrt
entries.notes: Unary elementwise functions take one block: exp, log, sqrt, rsqrt, recip, tanh, abs, neg, relu, sigmoid, silu, gelu. max and min take two.

entries.name: ttl.math.exp
entries.notes: Exponential of a block.

entries.name: ttl.math.silu
entries.notes: Activation for a gated MLP, fused with the multiply in one compute body.

entries.name: ttl.Pipe
entries.notes: A transfer from node src to one node or a range of nodes dst, in grid coordinates. One send reaches every node in the range (multicast).

entries.name: ttl.PipeNet
entries.notes: The set of pipes of one kernel. Make it before the main loop.

entries.name: PipeNet.if_src
entries.notes: Runs the callback on the sending node: the callback reads a block and sends it (ttl.copy from a block to the pipe).

entries.name: PipeNet.if_dst
entries.notes: Runs the callback on a receiving node: it copies from the pipe into a reserved block. Every if_dst callback must match one if_src callback.

entries.name: ttl.signpost
entries.notes: Marks a point for the profiler.

sections.title: Simulator-only forms (do not compile on the hardware package)

entries.name: sim.reduce_sum
entries.notes: The simulator requires shape and accepts this. The hardware package has no shape argument: `reduce_sum() got an unexpected keyword argument 'shape'`. 0 of 7 simulator-passing reduction kernels compiled on the chip (issue 205). Write the hardware form above.

entries.name: sim.fill
entries.notes: The simulator's ttl.block namespace (broadcast, fill, mask, where, squeeze, unsqueeze, transpose) is not in the hardware package; the hardware names live under ttl.math. Check the orchard kernel library before copying from it: its rmsnorm uses ttl.block and the shape argument.

entries.name: ttl.make_dfb
entries.notes: A buffer from a dtype with no backing tensor. Present in the newer tt-lang checkout, absent from the 1.1.6 hardware package; use make_dataflow_buffer_like there.

mistakes.symptom: `reduce_sum() got an unexpected keyword argument 'shape'` when a kernel that passed the simulator is compiled for the chip (issue 205).
mistakes.fix: Call ttl.math.reduce_sum(x, dims=[-1]) with no shape, then ttl.math.broadcast the result back. A simulator pass does not show the kernel compiles on hardware; for any reduction, read the hardware signature above.

mistakes.symptom: `@ttl.kernel` from older guides: the attribute does not exist.
`ttl.Semaphore` does not exist in the simulator or the package (issue 176): a kernel that synchronises with a semaphore cannot be checked.
mistakes.fix: Use dataflow buffers and pipes for synchronisation.

mistakes.symptom: The simulator's failures on coder kernels: a broadcast shape mismatch, `not a valid next dataflow step` after a pop, and a deadlock.
mistakes.fix: Each buffer has one producer and one consumer thread and both loop the same number of times; every wait has a matching reserve; a block is used inside its with block only. Start with copy through the buffers, add one arithmetic step, then the reduction, then the broadcast.

mistakes.symptom: A short depthwise convolution with dilation above 1 done with ttnn.conv1d returns a wrong result and no error (issue 338).
mistakes.fix: Write it as shifted multiply-adds (for kernel 4, dilation 3: sum over k of w[k] times x shifted by (3-k)*3), then the activation.
